searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — revelation map the awtsmoos renews the road and the reader, the date and the deed; awtsmoos.com should reveal one daily chumash portion with no duplicated creed. mission build daily chitas chumash study into the existing geelooy road read / heichel ikar system, using the project's real grouping model and existing torah text rather than a parallel interface. facts already observed repository root: work/awtsmoos.com. target web tree: work/awtsmoos.com/geelooy. root law requires inspection before claims and complete file rewrites only. geelooy contains heichel/, heichelos/, zmanim/, shared/, libs/, api/, and existing thought folders. unknowns to resolve from code 1. what the user means by “mc l” in heichel ikar and where that entity/alias is represented. 2. where the road read system calculates reading order, progression, and grouping. 3. what a “grouping” is in runtime data: schema, renderer, navigation, persistence, and url contract. 4. where torah/chumash content comes from and whether aliyah boundaries already exist. 5. whether the repository already has hebrew calendar, parsha, zmanim, or locale logic. 6. whether israel/diaspora parsha divergence is supported or must be modeled. 7. how holidays and double parshiyos affect the weekly seven aliyos and daily chitas split. 8. how the chabad chitas convention handles shabbos, yom tov, and rosh chodesh relative to the weekly sedra. research target the calculation must be deterministic from a civil date plus calendar mode/location. prefer a local algorithm and canonical metadata over scraping a daily page at runtime. external sources may be used to verify the rules and seed canonical aliyah boundaries. evidence gate no source file will be changed until the road read call path, grouping shape, text source, and calendar entry point are observed directly.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — architecture and file map the awtsmoos gives each boundary a vessel and each vessel a name; awtsmoos.com should let calendar, torah text, and road read meet without tangling the frame. candidate architecture to test against the repository a. calendar first resolver: date hebrew date weekly sedra weekday aliyah range. b. data first resolver: canonical annual calendar table date key sedra/aliyah metadata. c. provider first resolver: trusted external daily chitas endpoint normalized local grouping. d. hybrid resolver: local hebrew calendar/parsha calculation + canonical aliyah boundaries from existing torah metadata. e. heichel native resolver: use an existing grouping/progression plugin if road read already supports computed groups. preferred shape if the code supports it choose d + e: keep the heichel ui generic, add a small pure chitas calendar domain layer, and feed its result into the existing grouping abstraction. expected responsibilities calendar: determine jewish date and relevant weekly sedra in selected israel/diaspora mode. parsha: map sedra names/identifiers to seven aliyah boundaries. chitas: map weekday to the corresponding daily chumash span. adapter: translate the chitas span into the road read grouping schema. tests: verify ordinary weeks, double parshiyos, festival displacement, year boundary, israel/diaspora divergence, and sunday to shabbos sequence. files to touch unknown until tracing is complete. the final plan will enumerate exact observed paths only. no speculative source path will be created merely because this document names a responsibility. constraints complete file writes only. new modules should be small and focused. no runtime scraping if a deterministic local calculation is feasible. existing heichel routing/grouping conventions win over a new custom ui. chumash text should come from the project’s existing torah source where possible. a date calculation must make timezone/location policy explicit instead of relying on ambient browser utc.
